title: A key refusal is shown under the Listener row, and Remove's only there
body:
## Summary
Voice settings draws the one `saveError` the module keeps for a listener change, a key save and a key removal under the Listener row, so a refused OpenAI key (or a refused Remove) is reported beside the Whisper/OpenAI pills, away from the key.

## Description
modules/voice/live.ts sets `saveError` from three acts: `choose()` (live.ts:196, a listener or voice change), `saveKey` (live.ts:334) and `removeKey` (live.ts:342). apps/desktop/src/scenes/voice/settings.tsx:179 renders it under the Listener row, and the KeyField (modules/voice/pieces.tsx:120) renders it again only while the field is open. `OpenAiKey` closes the field the moment Save is pressed (settings.tsx:258 `onDone`), before the daemon answers, so a refused key always lands under Listener; a refused Remove (stored state, no field) is only ever there. The copy rule this breaks: a message that names the wrong place misdirects the remedy (the person re-picks a listener). Technique: software-engineering/form server-error-mapping (route a rejection into the slot that caused it). Fixed looks like the module keeping `keyError` apart from `saveError` (or tagging the act), settings drawing a key refusal under the OpenAI key row, and the Listener row drawing only a listener refusal.

## Flow
- settings, key stored -> Replace -> paste a malformed key -> Save key
- the field closes at once (onDone), the daemon refuses: validator_failed
- the refusal renders under Listener (settings.tsx:179), nothing under OpenAI key
- build: split the error in modules/voice/live.ts + model.ts (desktop-voice-ui context), then move the scene's two renderings; pin with a settings view test per act

## Expected impact
A person whose key was refused sees the reason next to the key and is not sent to the listener pills. Risk: the model's VoiceModel gains a field every consumer must pass (fixtures).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a refusal is shown where the act that caused it lives
Before: 3 acts share 1 error slot; 2 of 3 (save key after the field closes, remove key) render only under Listener
After: predicted 3 of 3 under their own row
Method: simulation - walked live.ts:196/334/342 against settings.tsx:179 and pieces.tsx:120; the split is in modules/voice (desktop-voice-ui), outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
modules/voice/live.ts:196 set({ saveError: `${out.reason}: ${refusalText(out)}` }); // choose() modules/voice/live.ts:334 set({ keyBusy: false, saveError: out.ok ? null : ... }); // saveKey modules/voice/live.ts:342 set({ keyBusy: false, saveError: out.ok ? null : ... }); // removeKey apps/desktop/src/scenes/voice/settings.tsx:179 {model.saveError ?

{model.saveError}

: null} // under Listener apps/desktop/src/scenes/voice/settings.tsx:258 setReplacing(false)} /> // closes before the answer
instrument: settings view test: a putKey refusal renders under the OpenAI key row and not under Listener, a choose refusal the reverse, after the module splits the error

title: The first act's Open it refusal is only console.error'd
body:
## Summary
When `tabs.create` refuses the address the first act opens, the setup module's openPage logs `[setup] open: ...` to the console and the first act shows nothing; the fact line stays "not yet · none open yet".

## Description
apps/desktop/src/modules/setup/index.ts:81 `openPage: (url) => void useTabs.getState().create(url).catch(report("open"))`, and `report` (index.ts:61) is `console.error`. Rust's tabs::create (src-tauri/src/tabs.rs:193) refuses an address `Url::parse` will not take and errors when the main window is gone. 91fd5c5 removed the commonest cause from the waking view (a bare host is now normalised, text with no origin is refused with a reason), but an address WHATWG URL accepts and the Rust parser or the webview builder refuses still fails into the console only. Technique: software-engineering/voice-io and async-ui-states failure-states (a failure must not render as the idle state); observability: a failure that changes the outcome leaves no trace the person can see. Fixed looks like openPage returning the refusal (or the setup model carrying an `openError`) and the first act drawing it under the field.

## Flow
- first act, Reach -> type an address Rust refuses -> Open it
- tabsCreate rejects -> report("open") -> console.error
- the step still reads "not yet · none open yet"; nothing says the open failed
- build: the setup module keeps the refusal (desktop-setup-module context), the waking view draws it beside the field

## Expected impact
A person whose first app did not open is told why on the step instead of seeing nothing happen. Risk: low; one new field on SetupModel.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a refused open is said where it was asked for
Before: 1 of 1 refusal paths ends in console.error only (index.ts:61,81)
After: predicted 0 silent paths
Method: simulation - walked index.ts:81 -> tabs.ts:37 -> tabs.rs:193; the seam is in modules/setup (desktop-setup-module), outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: setup model/hook test with a rejecting tabs.create asserting the refusal reaches the model, and a waking view test asserting it is drawn under the field

title: Voice says hold Ctrl+Shift+Space even when the shell failed to register it
body:
## Summary
The Voice field, the studio rail and ready card and settings all say "Talk anywhere: hold Ctrl+Shift+Space", but hotkeys.rs registers the chord non-fatally and, when another app owns it, only eprintln!s; no surface can know.

## Description
apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/hotkeys.rs:82-84 `if let Err(e) = manager.register(summon()) { eprintln!("[hotkeys] Ctrl+Shift+Space not registered: {e}"); }` ("Non-fatal: a chord another app already owns is reported and the app carries on", hotkeys.rs:70). No IPC command exposes the registration (grep hotkey in src/lib/ipc.ts and lib.rs: only `mod hotkeys` and `hotkeys::init`). The scene renders the chord unconditionally (scenes/voice/view.tsx Field footer, studio.tsx Rail foot and ReadyCard, settings.tsx bar). State-coverage: the degraded-dependency state (chord not held) renders exactly like the working one. Technique: software-engineering/voice-io voice-ux-integration (an affordance renders only when it can work or can explain itself). Fixed looks like Rust keeping the registration result, an IPC read of it, and the scene saying "the chord is held by another app" instead of the instruction when it is not registered.

## Flow
- another app owns Ctrl+Shift+Space -> Athena starts -> register fails -> eprintln only
- Voice -> settings: "Talk anywhere: hold Ctrl+Shift+Space. Let go and she answers."
- the person holds it: the other app acts, Athena does not
- build: hotkeys.rs records the result, a command returns it (lib.rs, capabilities, lib/ipc.ts), the scene reads it

## Expected impact
A person whose chord is taken is told so instead of being instructed to use a key that does nothing. Risk: a new IPC command (four hand-kept lists: build.rs, lib.rs, capabilities, ipc).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the chord instruction is shown only when the chord works
Before: 4 surfaces draw the instruction; 0 can see a failed registration
After: predicted 4 of 4 conditioned on the registration
Method: simulation - read hotkeys.rs:70-84 and the IPC surface; the change spans Rust and lib/ipc (desktop-shell-rust, desktop-client-lib), outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: cargo test that a failed register leaves an unregistered state, an ipc test for the read, and a voice view test that the instruction is replaced when the chord is not held

title: Her preview keeps speaking after the Voice place that played it is left
body:
## Summary
A voice preview started from the studio's pick step or settings' Play keeps playing when the person leaves the place (Escape rises, the dock goes home): nothing in the scene stops it on unmount, so audio outlives its surface.

## Description
Preview stops only on a studio move off the pick step (modules/voice/live.ts:215), a restart (live.ts:221), finish/reopen (live.ts:347,352) and the test reset; grep stopPreview in src outside tests finds no scene caller. The studio and settings unmount on a depth move while `preview.phase === "playing"`, the hero waveform's loop stops with them (no meter), and the voice goes on with nothing on screen that can stop it. Technique: software-engineering/voice-io tts-pipeline ("audio keeps playing after its surface is gone") and voice-ux-integration (the control that started speech is the control that stops it). Fixed looks like the place calling `actions.stopPreview()` on unmount when a preview is synthesising or playing (beside useTakeEndsWithPlace in scenes/voice/parts.tsx).

## Flow
- studio, pick step -> Play (or settings -> Play) -> Escape before she finishes
- the place unmounts; preview.phase stays playing; the audio runs to its end
- build: an unmount cleanup in the scene that calls stopPreview while synth or playing; pin with interact.test (unmount while speaking -> stopPreview)

## Expected impact
A person who leaves the voice place mid-preview gets silence with the surface, not a voice with no control. Risk: low; previews are a few seconds, and stopPreview is the module's own act.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - speech ends with the surface that started it
Before: 0 of 2 places (studio, settings) stop a playing preview on unmount
After: predicted 2 of 2
Method: simulation - grep of stopPreview callers and walked the depth move; not built this round for budget (the instrument is an S interact test)
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: voice/interact.test.tsx: mount the speaking fixture in the studio and in settings, unmount, expect stopPreview called once each; an idle place calls nothing
